note: The formula viewpoint asks whether polynomial-size bounded-fan-in Boolean circuits always have polynomial-size formulas. Under the standard AND/OR/NOT basis this is the nonuniform NC¹ versus P/poly frontier, using formula balancing to compare the models.

The older question discusses seed overhead in obtaining cryptographic pseudorandom generators from arbitrary one-way functions. It is retained as background for the linear-seed frontier, not asserted to be equivalent to every quantitative refinement in that discussion.

A super-log-cubed lower bound for three-party number-on-forehead disjointness is one specific milestone within the full communication-complexity problem. That threshold is preserved as context rather than a second independent target.
The qAC⁰ versus NL-complete dichotomy is a proposed coarse boundary in finite-semigroup membership. It is a component of the broader classification programme, not the complete classification itself.

A related restriction excludes both an induced long claw S_{t,t,t} and a fixed clique K_r, and asks for polynomial-time maximum-weight independent set for each fixed t,r. A theorem for that smaller graph class need not settle the general forbidden-long-claw question.

The weighted-automata source also invokes decidability of the first-order real field with exponentiation. It supplies an application of the same real-exponential theory question; the conditional role of Schanuel’s conjecture does not constitute an unconditional decision procedure.
This source asks whether ordinary word-equation satisfiability is in NP. The transferred question concerns plain equations over free monoids, without adding regular constraints or inversion.

The source asks whether complementing unambiguous automata over general alphabets can require exponential size. This is a proposed hard endpoint of the complementation gap, not an equivalent restatement of every weaker improvement target.
The AC⁰ classification is the shallow-circuit slice of the semigroup-membership classification. It should be distinguished from a complete classification across all complexity regimes.

The backdoor-defense source also raises efficient learning of polynomial-size decision trees from uniform random labeled examples. The access is random examples; free membership queries at selected inputs would change the learning problem.
This source raises the computability of graph Shannon capacity. The retained target asks for a uniform halting procedure at arbitrary requested precision, not just one fixed numerical tolerance.
The 2026 source again identifies NP membership of ordinary word-equation satisfiability as a frontier. It is retained with the plain-equation convention of this question.

This is an additional occurrence in the same CCC 2022 source of the heuristic-average-case hypothesis and its proposed subexponential consequence for UP. The oracle and time-bound quantifiers remain those of the retained conjecture.

The recompression survey discusses the complexity of plain word-equation satisfiability alongside extensions. Only its plain-equation question is consolidated here; regular-constraint extensions are not declared equivalent.

The S-only source distinguishes weak convertibility of closed terms from normalization and head-reduction termination. It also records that equal Berarducci trees need not imply convertibility, so that infinite-tree semantics alone does not decide the retained word problem.

The orbit-partition paper recalls the polynomial-time graph-isomorphism frontier and its connection with finding automorphism orbits. It is an application and equivalent computational viewpoint, not a separate unresolved graph-comparison target.
Sublogarithmic competitiveness of splay trees is a weaker quantitative milestone on the way to constant competitiveness. It is preserved as context and is not claimed to imply dynamic optimality.

This additional occurrence comes from the same compact-routing paper. The retained formal statement fixes its own girth threshold and graph-size quantifiers; a differently quantified girth conjecture is not automatically identified with it.
The potential-maximal-clique source also raises the complexity of exact treewidth on planar graphs, supplying another occurrence of the retained planar question.
The cubic-graph hardness source supplies context for the still separate planar treewidth problem. Hardness on cubic graphs alone does not establish hardness on planar graphs.

The source discusses deterministic prime construction. The retained card makes the bit-length parameter and polynomial bit-time output requirement explicit; primality testing a supplied number is a different task.

The earlier source asks for the integrality gap of the bidirected-cut relaxation for Steiner Tree. Its full quantitative target is broader than proving that the gap is strictly below two, so the two formulations are not declared equivalent.

Both introductory passages concern irrevocable bipartite matching of arriving clients to a known set of servers on the line, with sum of distances as cost and worst-case arrival order. Their deterministic O(log k) benchmark and deterministic constant-lower-bound discussion support the deterministic constant-competitive question. Randomized algorithms against oblivious adversaries form a distinct variant; the general-metric randomized discussion and recourse results are not substituted for a deterministic no-recourse guarantee.

The knowledge-compilation map asks for polynomial-time negation of deterministic DNNF and its smooth variant. This is constructive closure, including polynomial output size, and is stronger than nonconstructive polynomial-size closure; the latter remains separately represented by TCS-7260.

The 2023 source contains an earlier randomized weighted-k-server question. The 2026 upper bound supersedes the qualitative doubly-exponential barrier; its bibliography is retained here under the current optimal-ratio target.
